title: 2.4.5 Animated Sprites Sandbox
description: Drive a sprite's visual from input state — the same swap pattern used by addAni / changeAni, with sprite.image swapping as the asset-free placeholder. Idle when standing, run when moving, jump when 'w' is held.

steps.title: Create a player with an initial visual
steps.instructions: In setup(), create a sprite. Give it an idle visual — either sprite.image = '🧍' (emoji placeholder) or addAni('idle', 'img/idle.png') if you have art assets. The two forms swap the same way; we use sprite.image here because the in-app sandbox doesn't host image files.
hints: Open the shplay docs drawer and find the Visual / image section.

steps.title: Clear the background each frame
steps.instructions: Inside draw(), call background(...) at the top so old frames don't pile up.
hints: Search the shplay docs drawer for background().

steps.title: Read WASD input every frame
steps.instructions: Inside draw(), use kb.pressing('a') / 'd' / 'w' to read horizontal and jump-cue keys. Drive the player's horizontal motion (sprite.vel.x or sprite.x) from those checks.
hints: Open the shplay docs drawer and find the Input / Keyboard section.

steps.title: Swap the visual based on state
steps.instructions: When the player is moving horizontally, swap sprite.image to a 'run' emoji (e.g. '🏃'). While 'w' is held, swap to a 'jump' emoji (e.g. '🤸'). Otherwise, swap back to idle. Don't forget the else branch — without it the visual won't reset. (With real art, this is changeAni('run') / changeAni('idle') / changeAni('jump').)
hints: Open the shplay docs drawer and find the Visual / image section. Single emoji strings work as visuals.

requirements.title: Player sprite has a visual
requirements.description: Assign sprite.image (or sprite.img) somewhere in your sketch.

requirements.title: Two or more visual states
requirements.description: Either register multiple animations with addAni, OR assign sprite.image to at least two different values across the file.

requirements.title: Visual swap driven by input
requirements.description: Inside draw(), assign sprite.image (or call changeAni) inside or in response to a kb.pressing check.
